subject: Re: FinCo performance SLOs — context window & latency follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:06:00 -0700
Subject: FinCo call recap — perf targets, context window, next steps

Alex / Sara — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on perf/production constraints: 

Summary of requirements you called out:
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 350ms for single-request chat completions (streaming allowed)
- Throughput: sustained 120 reqs/sec with spikes to 250 reqs/sec during batch jobs
- Concurrency: up to 60 concurrent active streams (chat sessions)
- Context window: ~32k input tokens (historical chat + metadata) with up to 2k output tokens
- Streaming: required for UX — partial tokens should arrive <120ms after generation begins

Questions / notes from our side:
- Context windows of 32k strongly influence memory & KV cache sizing; we typically recommend a hybrid approach (local short-term KV + cold store for full history) to keep downstream latency low.
- Large input windows + long outputs will push model choices toward high-memory variants and may require quantization/partitioning to stay within latency SLO.
- For your p95 target with streaming, we should validate on representative prompts. The attached performance sheet includes a few estimate scenarios (start with the v1 estimates).

Next steps proposed:
1) You to send 3 representative chat transcripts (anonymized) and a typical request rate profile (CSV).
2) We will run an internal micro-benchmark (2 configs: batching-optimized and streaming-optimized) and share p50/p95/p99 and tail traces. Expect ~4 business days.
3) Post-benchmark sync with your infra lead to discuss dedicated capacity vs hosted routing.

Attachments: redwood-performance-sheet.xlsx (initial sizing / latency estimates), SLA-draft.pdf (enterprise SLA language).

Thanks — I copied Dev and Rishi for technical follow-up.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Lee <sara.lee@finco.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinCo call recap — perf targets, context window, next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) When we say 32k context tokens, ~80% is short-term history (~25k) and ~20% are long-running knowledge/context (~7k). We can trim non-critical metadata server-side if that helps.
2) Streaming: our product UX expects the first partial token within 150ms of request acceptance for 95% of cases — is the 120ms number you mentioned an internal target or requirement? We can relax to 150ms if that's easier.
3) For throughput: the 120 rps baseline is for peak business hours; background batch enrichment will run overnight and can be queued — so spikes to 250 are short-lived (~30 mins).

We will provide the transcripts and the request profile by EOD Wednesday. Also looping in our infra lead, Sara (cc'd). Can you confirm the benchmark setup you plan to run (model variants, hardware assumptions)?

—Alex
Product Lead, Integrations — FinCo
alex.johnson@finco.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinCo call recap — perf targets, context window, next steps

Alex / Sara — thanks for the details. Quick note on benchmark config so expectations are aligned: 

Planned micro-benchmark (two tracks):
- Streaming-optimized: medium-sized model variant with streaming-enabled I/O, KV cache warmed for short-term history (25k tokens), deployment on DGX-class GPUs (A100 equivalent), continuous batching disabled to prioritize lower tail latency.
- Batching-optimized: larger model variant with aggressive batching and micro-batching windows (to maximize throughput and lower token cost) on pool of T4-like instances for sustained 120 rps. This will accept slightly higher p95 but lower cost.

Metrics we'll report: p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end server-side latency (token-first-byte and completion), token throughput, CPU/GPU utilization, and memory/KV footprint.

Assumptions:
- 32k context will require model sharding / KV overflows to remote cache for the largest transcripts; that can add additional 30-120ms depending on hit rate.
- We expect to hit your p95 350ms target on streaming-optimized config for typical prompts (shorter responses). For worst-case long outputs (2k tokens) the completion time will exceed the 350ms SLO but initial streaming packets should meet the partial-token window.

We'll document everything in the benchmark report and include tail traces. If you want, we can include a third config that uses dedupe-prioritization (trim non-essential system tokens) to see how much latency savings you get on average.

—Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

From: Sara Lee <sara.lee@finco.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finco.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinCo call recap — perf targets, context window, next steps

Thanks — that level of detail is helpful. A few quick asks before you run the benchmark: 

- Please include a test that simulates 60 concurrent long-lived streams (chat sessions) while also handling a 200 rps burst for 2 minutes. We want to ensure the routing and KV cache behavior under combined stress.
- For the streaming-optimized run, can you measure first-byte latency and time-to-first-meaningful-token (TTFMT) separately? Those two numbers matter a lot for our UX team.
- Can you provide a rough cost delta estimate between the streaming-optimized and batching-optimized configs? Ballpark is fine.

We'll upload the transcripts and the request profile to the Drive link you provided by EOD Wednesday. Looking forward to the benchmark report.

—Sara
Infra Lead, FinCo
